svg.title: A logarithm is its exponential reflected over y = x
svg.desc: Two curves and a straight diagonal line. The steeply rising curve is two to the power x; the slowly rising one is the logarithm base two of x; the diagonal is the line y equals x. The two curves are mirror images of each other in that diagonal. Reflecting a point over y equals x swaps its coordinates, so a point at one comma two on the exponential corresponds to a point at two comma one on the logarithm. That is what makes the two functions inverses: the exponential's outputs are the logarithm's inputs and the other way round. The logarithm is drawn only for positive inputs, because that is its whole domain.
svg.text: If (s, t) lies on bˣ then (t, s) lies on logᵇ x
Reflecting over y = x swaps the coordinates: (s, t) becomes (t, s).
